lines.text: Listen. A police chief on a small island in the Indian Ocean hears heavy guns, roaring far off to the east.
lines.cue: caption: HEAVY GUNS, FAR TO THE EAST

lines.text: The date: the twenty-seventh of August, eighteen eighty-three.
The booms come back every few hours, until three in the afternoon.
But there are no guns. Whatever is making that noise is almost three thousand miles away.
That's about four thousand eight hundred kilometres. Sound needs around four hours to cross that much ocean.
And it wasn't only him. People in Perth, about three thousand kilometres away, heard it too.
lines.cue: caption: PERTH HEARD IT TOO, ~3,000 KM

lines.text: Draw the whole area where it was heard on a map, and it covers nearly one thirteenth of the planet's surface.
So what makes a sound that crosses an ocean? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
